item.title: Water in kimberlitic olivine provides insights into kimberlite ascent and diamond transport
item.dc:creator: Soumendu Sarkar
Rondi M. Davies

Luísa D. V. Carvalho

item.description: This study links higher diamond grades in kimberlites to water-rich olivine. Modeling suggests that rapid magma ascent preserves higher olivine water contents and facilitates efficient diamond transport, highlighting ascent rate as a key control on diamond preservation. Kimberlites are volatile-rich magmas that transport diamonds from the deep lithosphere to the surface, yet the exact processes controlling their variable diamond abundances remain debated. Compiled dataset of water contents in mantle olivine shows that kimberlites containing water-rich (>40 wt. ppm) olivine exhibit higher diamond grades. Diffusion modeling coupled with estimates of the ascent velocities of olivine xenocrysts indicate that preserved water in the cores of olivine crystals reflects variable magma ascent rates. High water contents are indicative of rapid ascent that not only limits hydrogen loss but also leads to enhanced diamond transport. Conversely, slower ascent promotes olivine dehydration and reduction in diamond-carrying capacity. The link between olivine water content and diamond grade highlights that ascent rate is a key factor in controlling the varied diamond abundance in kimberlites. Water in olivine thus provides an additional, complementary, and cost-effective proxy for estimating kimberlite ascent and diamond-carrying efficiency. item.description: Subduction recycles surface materials into the mantle and shapes its chemical evolution. Whether continental subduction leaves chalcophile-element imprints in the mantle that differ from those of oceanic subduction remains poorly understood. Here, we show that primitive basaltic magmas from the North China Craton exhibit pronounced copper depletion, silver enrichment, and low copper/silver (200 to 1200), together with continental crust–like trace element patterns and radiogenic-isotope compositions. These features contrast sharply with those of the convective mantle, mid-ocean ridge basalts, and oceanic arc basalts, and reflect chemical signatures inherited from subducted continental crust and retained over geological timescales in metasomatized domains of a relatively cold lithospheric mantle. Coupled lead enrichment and unradiogenic lead-isotope signatures further identify metasomatized mantle as an important reservoir of Earth’s unradiogenic lead. Our results reveal distinct modes of chalcophile-element recycling and mantle inheritance during continental and oceanic subduction, with broad implications for mantle chemical evolution and the critical-metal fertility of continental lithosphere. item.dc:creator: Gerardo Dominguez

item.prism:publicationName: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
item.description: Mass-independent isotope fractionation (MIF) of oxygen provides key insights into atmospheric chemistry and the origin of isotopic anomalies in planetary materials. To date, MIF has been primarily associated with gas-phase processes involving symmetry-dependent reaction pathways, most notably ozone formation. Whether analogous effects can arise in condensed phases or at interfaces remains an open question. Here we report laboratory experiments demonstrating that energetic particle irradiation of icy oxide surfaces produces mass-independent oxygen isotope fractionation at temperatures as low as 10 K. Electron irradiation of SiO 2 and Al 2 O 3 substrates in the presence of H 2 O ice results in measurable shifts in Δ 17 O in the underlying solids. The resulting three-isotope relationships include slope-1-like behavior in SiO 2 and Al 2 O 3 and distinct, substrate-dependent trends in Al 2 O 3 , indicating that irradiation-induced defect formation and interfacial chemistry govern the isotope effects. The magnitude of the observed anomalies demonstrates that irradiation-driven processes can generate substantial oxygen isotope heterogeneity in condensed phases. These results identify a previously unrecognized class of MIF and provide a quantitative framework for interpreting oxygen isotope signatures in radiation-processed environments, including interstellar grains and early solar system materials. item.description: Metamorphic proteins challenge the single-sequence-structure-function paradigm by switching between distinct folds that often adopt complementary functions. However, the conformational states sampled along the fold-switching pathway have remained elusive because they are transient and unstable. Using multinuclear chemical exchange saturation transfer and relaxation dispersion NMR, combined with chemical shift–based structure determination and protein engineering, we visualized the atomic resolution structure of an “invisible” state of the metamorphic chemokine lymphotactin. This state is a chimera that integrates the secondary and tertiary structure of one fold with the quaternary assembly of the other. Locking lymphotactin into a single conformation abolishes access to this state, supporting its role as an on-pathway intermediate in metamorphosis. The stabilization of such hybrid intermediates is likely to have facilitated the evolution of fold-switching and represents a powerful strategy for protein design. item.title: Effusive sedimentary volcanism experimentally reproduced under Martian-like conditions
item.dc:creator: Ondřej Krýza
Petr Brož
Jacob Adler
Matthew Sylvest
Manish Patel
item.description: Abstract Rapid boiling, cooling, and freezing are commonly assumed to rapidly quench metastable liquid eruptions exposed to near-vacuum planetary environments, influencing both sedimentary volcanism on Mars and cryovolcanism on icy worlds. However, how these coupled phase transitions govern eruptive processes remains largely unknown. Here we show experimentally that boiling instead sustains coupled ballistic-effusive mud eruptions under Martian-like pressure conditions (~4.5 mbar). Using an ice-sealed metastable reservoir, we reproduced subsurface-driven eruptions initiated by internally generated boiling-induced overpressure. Eruptions evolved systematically from short-lived ballistic fountains toward episodic effusive emplacement accompanied by coherent mud-flow formation. Ballistic transport redistributed liquid mud around the vent and promoted proximal accumulation that subsequently coalesced into sustained flows despite ongoing cooling and freezing. Numerical modeling further demonstrates that erupted mud would remain largely unfrozen during ballistic transport under Martian gravity conditions. Together, our results show that rapid boiling does not suppress sedimentary volcanism under low-pressure conditions, but instead actively sustains eruptive transport and surface emplacement. These findings provide new constraints on this process on Mars and establish a broader physical framework for metastable liquid eruptions across the Solar System. item.description: Abstract Offshore freshened groundwater (OFG) is a significant yet underexplored component of the global water cycle, and its spatial distribution, particularly its links to past glacial processes, remains poorly constrained. The southeastern North Sea, characterized by extensive tunnel valley networks, provides an ideal setting to test how Pleistocene meltwater shaped offshore groundwater systems. Using newly acquired time-domain controlled-source electromagnetic data integrated with high-resolution seismic reflection surveys, we present a resistivity-based mapping of OFG in this region. The models reveal a laterally continuous OFG body with resistivities of 8–14 Ω·m, extending across multiple stratigraphic units and well beyond individual subglacial landforms. This configuration is best explained by subglacial meltwater flushing of sediment porewaters during Pleistocene glaciations. Subsequent preservation was aided by density contrasts that limit vertical mixing and by fine-grained glaciomarine deposits sealing the system from above. The connection between resistivity anomalies and mapped subglacial landforms shows that the latter can serve as predictive proxies for OFG occurrence. These findings shift the perspective from OFG as isolated anomalies to regionally extensive systems linked to glacial processes, establishing subglacial landforms as a testable screening proxy for locating OFG in formerly glaciated margins worldwide. item.description: Continuous seismic observations and numerical simulations reveal that, over the past decade, fluid migration and microseismic responses at The Geysers geothermal field have been primarily controlled by heterogeneous permeability. Fracture networks directly govern the efficiency of geothermal energy extraction and play a critical role in fluid migration and microearthquake generation. Using deep learning and Markov clustering, we build a high-resolution microseismic catalog covering the past decade for The Geysers geothermal field, California. Our observations reveal distinctive clustering patterns and inferred fracture systems tightly correlated with injection operations. Source mechanism analyses and pore pressure simulations indicate that the inferred connected fracture network provides pathways for rapid and directional pore pressure diffusion, highlighting that heterogeneous permeability controls the localized migration of fluids and the associated microseismic response. Our study highlights the importance of continuous and integrated seismic monitoring for ensuring the sustainability of long-term reservoir development and exploitation. item.description: The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar ε Nd values (∼−5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic ε Nd (∼−10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the ε Nd signature of the fish’s living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins. item.description: Vegetation greening and abrupt permafrost thaw are reshaping sediment dynamics across the Tibetan Plateau, yet their relative effects on sediment delivery remain poorly quantified. Here we show that retrogressive thaw slumps are disproportionately important sediment sources, with erosion rates two to three orders of magnitude above undisturbed landscapes and source-to-channel connectivity generally exceeding 60%. Combining multi-decadal satellite observations, high-resolution topographic differencing and cold-region hydrological modelling, we quantify the competing effects of thaw-slump sediment supply and greening-induced erosion reduction. During 2000–2022, thaw slumps delivered more than four times as much non-ice sediment to channels as was reduced by greening, compensating for declining glacier-derived sediment and contributing to increased downstream suspended sediment export. item.description: The eastern section of the northern margin of the North China Craton hosts diverse Ag-polymetallic deposits; however, the Aohan district has historically been dominated by gold mineralization. item.title: Tectono-stratigraphic evolution of the Jura-Cretaceous Wrangell-Nutzotin-Dezadeash basin and the Cretaceous Chisana-Blanchard River basin: A long-term record of subduction polarity reversal and Magmatic Arc Migration in the Northern Cordillera of Alaska, U.S.A., and Yukon, Canada

item.description: Two working hypotheses explain the tectonic evolution of the collage of geologic elements comprising the Northern Cordillera of Alaska and Yukon: a long-term eastward subduction scenario and a westward-then-eastward subduction scenario. item.description: The Triassic platform carbonates of the Eastern and Southern Alps host over 500 Pb-Zn deposits collectively known as Alpine-type (AT) Pb-Zn deposits. Syn-ore carbonates show a distinctive geochemical signature (Fe and Mn enrichment) and constrain the mineralization to a short interval in the Late Triassic (214.0 ± 5.8 Ma to 205.2 ± 3.3 Ma). These constraints support a revised genetic model involving Late Triassic mobilization of oxidized, metal-bearing brines sourced from Permian clastic units (i.e. Val Gardena Sandstone and the Sesto Conglomerate) during early regional extension and strike-slip tectonic. item.description: Field, petrographic, and isotopic data indicate that the compositionally zoned lithium-caesium‑tantalum (LCT) pegmatites in the thermal aureole of the Adamello batholith (Italian Alps) formed by low degrees of anatexis of metasedimentary rocks. item.description: As one of the most pivotal continental blocks in Southeast Asia, the South China Block (SCB) hosts globally significant ore systems and serves as a natural laboratory for studying intracontinental polymetallic mineralization. The model reveals pronounced multi-scale heterogeneity in the lithospheric electrical structure, characterized by distinct vertical stratification and lateral discontinuity. The Yangtze Block is characterized by high resistivity (>103 Ω·m) as the dominant feature, while the eastern Cathaysia Block contains several prominent crustal-scale conductors (C6, C7, C8) overlain on moderately resistive lithospheric mantle (102-103 Ω·m). In general, the crustal conductors in the eastern SCB support the interpretation of lithospheric dehydration-induced thermal erosion. This process facilitated the ascent of deep-sourced fluids through Late Mesozoic magmatic channels into the upper crust, thereby enhancing crustal conductivity and establishing effective crust-mantle material exchange. Such spatial correspondence between lower-crustal conductors and lithospheric thinning zones further reinforces this mechanism. Meanwhile, our findings align best with a dynamic model tied to the Meso-Cenozoic subduction of the Paleo-Pacific Plate. The tectonic sequence involves initial lithospheric thickening during flat-slab subduction, subsequent large-scale asthenospheric upwelling during slab rollback, and final regional extension and lithospheric thinning driven by slab break-off. This tectonic evolution fostered the formation of a rejuvenated lithosphere and extensive magmatic-minerogenetic systems, while further controlling regional metallogenic distribution through large-scale crust-mantle interactions that remelted both ancient and juvenile crust. In addition, translithospheric fault systems act as conduits for asthenospheric materials and fluid circulation, directly regulating the spatial distribution and metal assemblages of major ore belts to reflect variable shallow responses to deep dynamic processes. item.title: From molecular pathways to petrographic textures: A new framework for carbonate mineralization and structural evolution
item.dc:creator: Qiang Li
Chao Han
item.description: Carbonate minerals are fundamental components of the sedimentary record, yet their mineralogical and textural diversity cannot be understood from equilibrium thermodynamics or any single crystallization model alone. This review develops an evidence-constrained, pathway-dependent framework that links carbonate nucleation, growth and transformation processes with environmental modulation, structural inheritance, and their expression in the sedimentary record. We distinguish prenucleation solution states from condensed-phase formation and subsequent growth, treating stable prenucleation clusters as a debated model, while integrating ion-by-ion growth, liquid–liquid phase separation, amorphous precursors, particle-mediated growth, and oriented attachment within a common pathway framework. Environmental variables-including supersaturation, temperature, ionic composition, organic matter, EPS, and microbial activity-jointly bias the accessibility, persistence, and transformation of these pathways. Crystallization histories may generate nanoscale structural and compositional features that are selectively inherited by larger-scale carbonate textures; however, pathway–mineral–texture relationships are non-unique, and robust interpretation requires convergent mineralogical, crystallographic, microstructural, geochemical, temporal, and environmental evidence. Applied to the dolomite problem, this framework emphasizes multiple, system-dependent routes by which kinetic barriers to Mg incorporation and Ca–Mg ordering may be overcome, rather than a universal precursor sequence. Together, these elements define an evidence-constrained, non-deterministic pathway–mineral–texture framework that integrates molecular- to nanoscale crystallization processes with environmental modulation, selective structural inheritance, and diagenetic modification, allowing crystallization histories to be evaluated through convergent evidence rather than inferred from mineral identity or texture alone. item.description: Abstract Numerous seismic studies have reported the absence of a resolvable subducted slab beneath parts of northern Kamchatka, though the mechanism for this anomaly remains debated. item.description: The Eastern Himalayan Syntaxis (EHS) exhibits some of the world’s fastest exhumation rates, but the mechanisms driving its evolution remain debated. item.description: Quantifying sulfur (S) speciation in apatite‐group minerals (apatites) is critically important for understanding magmatic and magmatic‐hydrothermal processes but has generally been restricted to individual analytical techniques. In this study, we have quantified sulfur speciation in a suite of apatites (including fluorapatite, hydroxylapatite and chlorapatite) using three complementary analytical techniques: S K ‐edge X‐ray absorption near‐edge structure (XANES), S 2 p X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and S K α wavelengths with electron probe micro analysis (EPMA). Sulfur K ‐edge XANES offers the most precise quantification of S 6+ /ΣS values (where ΣS = S 6+ + S 4+ + S 2‐ ) from 0.93 to 1.0, with the standard deviation from ±0.01 to ±0.06, although it requires synchrotron access and careful calibration. Sulfur 2 p XPS analyses yield a similar trend in S speciation but lower S 6+ /ΣS values from 0.69 to 0.78, attributable to partial radiation‐induced reduction of S 6+ to S 4+ related to prolonged X‐ray exposure. Similarly, the EPMA‐based (S K α wavelength shift) technique is capable of distinguishing between S 6+ and S 4+ , and yields S 6+ /ΣS values ranging from 0.56 to 0.88, again indicating significant radiation‐induced reduction. Therefore, the XPS and EPMA‐based techniques are also capable of quantifying sulfur speciation in apatites but require accurate corrections for radiation‐induced sulfur reduction. This study highlights the strengths and limitations of these three analytical techniques, with XANES offering the highest sensitivity. At the same time, XPS and EPMA, although less sensitive, are surface‐specific and widely accessible, respectively. It also guides their applications for quantifying sulfur speciation in apatites. item.description: Extreme hydroclimatic changes linked to greenhouse gas emissions from large igneous provinces are exemplified by the Carnian Pluvial Episode (CPE; ca. 233 Ma), during which volcanic activity drove shifts in the hydrological cycle, though marine records offer only indirect evidence of terrestrial changes. Still, the reliability of the data is difficult to evaluate, due to the absence of detailed sampling and information on mechanisms. The most obvious episode of Hg enrichment and negative carbon isotope excursions during interval I is consistent with massive releases of local volcanogenic Hg and carbon to the Earth-surface system. Within the CPE interval, carbon isotope and sedimentary records indicate that the latter two pulses of depleted carbon into the atmosphere–lacustrine system were linked to discrete enhancements of the hydrological cycle. item.description: Abstract Integrating multiple detrital mineral systems provides a powerful framework for reconstructing source‐region tectonothermal evolution because different minerals record complementary aspects of magmatic and metamorphic processes. Detrital apatite records dominant mafic and I‐type magmatism between ∼970 and 650 Ma, with more evolved peraluminous signatures appearing at 850–820 Ma, broadly consistent with declining zircon εHf(t) values. Detrital rutile reveals dominant Neoproterozoic (∼970–790 Ma) and subordinate Paleoproterozoic (2.2–1.8 Ga) metamorphic signatures. Zr‐in‐rutile thermometry indicates temperatures of 480°C–980°C, including a distinct ∼950–820 Ma high‐pressure, low‐temperature population consistent with blueschist‐ to eclogite‐facies conditions. These data record major tectonic transitions within the Panxi‐Hannan orogen of the northwestern Yangtze Block, from an intra‐oceanic arc (970–880 Ma) to a continental arc (870–790 Ma), followed by regional extension after 790 Ma. The cessation of rutile and metamorphic apatite ages coincides with the onset of regional extension in the source orogen. The ∼950–820 Ma cold‐subduction signature expands the global record of Tonian low‐geothermal‐gradient metamorphism. Our results demonstrate that integrating multiple detrital mineral systems yields a more complete tectonic history than any single provenance proxy.
